title: Redaction workshop — customer training & runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the notes and an operational runbook from the customer-facing redaction workshop we ran for a mid-sized fintech POC. Goal: give the SE and SRE teams a repeatable checklist and automation options to ensure interactive sessions (chat, live transcripts, demo calls) do not persist customer PII beyond agreed retention windows and are auditable for compliance reviews.

Scope & assumptions:
- Scope is interactive POC sessions run using Redwood Hosted API or Dedicated pools; also covers customer Private installs where the control plane can be limited.
- We assume customers may want: (a) ephemeral session transcripts that are never written to durable storage; (b) short TTL retention (e.g., 24h) with KMS-scoped keys; (c) automated PII redaction on ingest for telemetry and logs.
- Not in scope: full product-level DPA wording (legal), or long-term analytics pipelines (those are separate).

Threat model (quick):
- Accidental persistence of PII in logs, debug traces, or cached KV stores.
- Operator error misconfiguring retention TTLs.
- Cross-tenant leakage from telemetry ingestion if scrubbers mis-routed.
- Customer asking to revert redaction for debugging (we must have deny-by-default).

Workshop outcomes (summary):
- Agreed canonical options with customers: ephemeral-only, short-ttl-with-audit, and scrubbed-telemetry modes. Customer selected short-ttl-with-audit for the pilot.
- Implementation plan: routing proxy + streaming scrub hook + post-session sweep + immutable audit record for redaction actions.
- Action item: produce a sample redaction config and a hands-on lab for customers.

Architecture patterns discussed (ops-friendly):
1) Proxy-scrub model (recommended for hosted/Dedicated POCs):
   - Ingress -> Redwood scrub-proxy (stateless) -> runtime
   - Scrub-proxy applies deterministic regex + ML entity detection (PII models) on streams, masks tokens, forwards both masked and an encrypted metadata envelope to short-lived KV only.
   - No persistent transcript stored in primary DB unless explicitly requested.
2) Streaming redact + audit trail:
   - Live stream is redacted in-memory before tokenization; raw tokens are never written to disk.
   - Event: redact action emits audit record (hash of session id, redaction policy id, timestamp) to audit log (WORM storage with KMS key).
3) Post-session sweep (for Dedicated/private installs):
   - Keep session artifacts in ephemeral tier for TTL (configurable, default 24h).
   - A background job runs a scrub-and-delete sweep, emitting a signed delete receipt into audit logs.

Operational runbook (pre-engagement):
- Pre-engagement checklist for SEs:
  1. Confirm customer retention profile and legal ask (ephemeral / 24h / 30d etc.) and capture in JIRA ticket.
  2. Determine deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private). If Private, confirm KMS/HSM integration and network egress policies.
  3. Choose redaction policy profile (strict / moderate / monitoring-only). Default to strict for fintech.
  4. Provision a scrub-proxy for the pilot (we use poctools/scrub-proxy v0.3 for trials).
  5. Share the runbook & lab link with customer: CONFLUENCE-6789.

Operational runbook (during session):
- Live checklist for operator oncall (SE/SRE):
  1. Start session under an isolated session-id (session-YYYYMMDD-cust).
  2. Verify scrub-proxy logging level: REDACT and AUDIT enabled.
  3. Confirm that telemetry endpoint returns masked tokens (spot-check 3 samples).
  4. If the customer requests debug raw transcripts, escalate to legal & product — deny by default until signed exception.
  5. Monitor real-time metrics: token ingestion rate, scrub latency (SLO < 25ms), redaction false-positive % (target < 1%).

Operational runbook (post-session):
- Post-session teardown & verification: 
  1. Immediately trigger post-session sweep job (if TTL=0).
  2. For TTL > 0, ensure retention TTL configured on ephemeral store (S3 lifecycle rule or DB TTL).
  3. Validate audit record: audit-log contains session-hash, policy id, redaction checksum, delete receipt if applicable.
  4. Run a sampling job (script: scripts/verify_no_raw.sh) to ensure no raw transcripts exist in backups or snapshots.
  5. Close the JIRA with pointers to the audit artifacts.

Automation options & scripts (notes for SEs):
- poctools/scrub-proxy: can run as a sidecar or standalone container. Env args: REDACT_LEVEL=strict, AUDIT_SINK=https://audit.internal/ingest, KMS_KEY=arn:aws:kms:...
- verify_no_raw.sh (simple grep + checksum): run across s3 buckets and DB snapshot exports, returns non-zero if raw tokens appear.
- delete_receipt_signer: small lambda that takes session-id and returns signed delete proof stored in WORM bucket.

Sample monitoring/alerting settings to push to SRE: 
- Alert when scrub latency > 50ms sustained for 1m.
- Alert when audit sink failures > 5 per 5m.
- Daily report: number of sessions, number of redaction events, top 5 PII categories matched.

Teaching/training plan (for customer workshop):
1.  15m primer on risk and options (ephemeral vs TTL vs scrubbed analytics).
2.  45m hands-on: deploy scrub-proxy locally, run a demo session with seeded PII, observe scrubbed vs raw behavior.
3.  30m teardown: review audit artifacts and run verify_no_raw.sh.
4.  15m next-steps and Q&A.

Open questions / unresolved decisions captured during workshop:
- Backups: customer asked whether backups of ephemeral stores could contain raw transcripts. Action: identify all backup paths, enumerate and add explicit TTL/lifecycle or scrub them. (Owner: Rana)
- KMS scoping: customer wants customer-managed key per pilot. Action: confirm KMS policy template for Private and Dedicated. (Owner: Eliot)
- Redaction rule transparency: customer requested a copy of the deterministic regex rules. We agreed to provide a high-level summary but not full list (security). Product to produce redaction-summary doc. (Owner: Tomás)

Customer-facing artifacts to produce (action items):
- POCTECH-84: deliver sample scrub-proxy manifest + env var guide (ETA 2025-09-05) — assignee: Maya
- POCTECH-85: produce hands-on lab deck and scripts (ETA 2025-09-09) — assignee: Eliot
- POCTECH-86: audit receipt signer and sample verification script (ETA 2025-09-12) — assignee: SRE

Appendix — sample redact policy (human-readable):
- Policy name: fintech-strict-2025
- Intents: remove all tokens labeled as: SSN, PAN, BANK_ACC, DOB, EMAIL, PHONE; mask partial tokens (first 2, last 2 chars) for investigatory logs only; telemetry events keep counts only, not value.

Appendix — example operator Slack message template (to customer during teardown):
"Hi @<customer-team>, the pilot session <session-id> completed. We have applied 'fintech-strict-2025' redaction and retained artifacts for 24h in ephemeral-only storage. Audit receipt: audit://signed-delete/<receipt-id>. Reach out if you need the audit export (requires legal approval)."

Notes & lessons learned from this workshop (quick):
- Customers understand TTLs but expect human-readable receipts; prioritize readable audit exports.
- False positives in regex-based scrubbers blocked some telemetry; ML-backed entity detectors should be in the loop to reduce business-impacting FP.
- For Private installs we must provide a one-click KMS integration checklist; otherwise operators forget to rotate keys and expirations.

References:
- CONFLUENCE-6789 (workshop deck)
- JIRA-SEQ-412 (pilot retention ticket)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poctools/pull/84

If you are the SE assigned to a pilot: use this doc as the canonical runbook. Update the checklist items with the customer-specific retention numbers and attach the signed DPA addendum to the JIRA before kickoff.

-- end of draft --
